deliverables: Intersect budget administration, audit, oversight, reporting obligations, and milestone-based disbursement controls
request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v, submitted by Intersect on behalf of the vendor Teragone
request.what: Withdraw treasury funds for Mithril Protocol continuous development and Intersect administration.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 3,810,423 ada, consisting of 3,699,440 ada for Mithril Protocol Continuous Development and 110,983 ada for the Intersect Budget Administration fee.
Mithril uses stake-based threshold multi-signatures to certify Cardano state in a trustless way, enabling nodes and applications to verify state rapidly without relying on the entire chain.
Full node synchronisation is currently slow and light clients rely on centralized trust, creating a pressing Cardano infrastructure challenge.

Funding Mithril's continued development through Intersect MBO is presented as necessary for Cardano to scale while preserving decentralization guarantees and avoiding dependency on centralized indexers and hosted APIs.

The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain submission under the approved Budget Process Framework.
The requested withdrawal does not, at submission time, on its own or in aggregate, breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.
Independent oversight will be provided through Intersect and technically capable third parties, with reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls.
Teragone has not previously received direct funding from Cardano treasury or community governance programs, while prior Mithril work was funded by IOG.
Intersect will administer the funds using a Sundae Labs treasury management smart contract framework with listed TRSC and PSSC addresses and specified multisignature authorization rules.
A public dashboard and on-chain records are available for the community to audit the TRSC or PSSC and track metrics related to the withdrawn ada.

summary: The document asks for 3,810,423 ada for Mithril Protocol development via Intersect, citing infrastructure benefits, Intersect budget-process approval, NCL compliance, smart-contract custody, oversight controls, and audit/dashboard references.
